Original abstract

We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on , we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, satisfying , is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists.

Original abstract

We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space . We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function has bounded support in , there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of , where is the smallest natural number such that for every . For , results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of , where is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

Ambient Chain-Relation Reduction in Contracting Controlled Skew-Product Semiflows

Relevance

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

The qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations is often studied through cocycles and skew-product semiflows over a driving base. We develop a chain-recurrence reduction principle for systems admitting an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking. The abstract theorem determines the complete chain-attainability relation in the ambient phase space: chains may start off the attracting section, but every attainable target lies on it and is selected solely by the factor semiflow. Applied to contracting controlled skew-product semiflows, this gives exact descriptions of the chain recurrent set, chain components, Conley order, compact strictly invariant sets, attractors, basins, and dual repellers. A weighted-supremum transverse gauge yields a complete Lyapunov function for the full semiflow while preserving the recurrent values of the base. The differential hypotheses are verified through subadditive fiber-derivative growth and averaged moving-metric logarithmic norms, allowing transient expansion and non-unique ergodicity. Quantitative persistence is established for finite-window maps and smooth vector-field perturbations. The results provide a unified framework for chain recurrence, Lyapunov structure, and attractor–repeller geometry in contracting nonautonomous dynamics.

Original abstract

We are developing some topological dynamics below a given ambit. We define and study Bohr compactifications below ambits and other related objects. We describe a natural epimorphism from the Ellis group of an ambit to the Bohr compactification below its Ellis semigroup ambit. The first main result says that, assuming tameness and hereditary amenability, this natural map is an isomorphism of topological groups. This is an abstract dynamical generalization of Newelski's conjecture, or rather a theorem of Chernikov and Simon that a natural map from the Ellis group of the flow to the definable Bohr compactification of is an isomorphism when is a definably amenable group definable in a NIP structure . We give two proofs of our main result: a shorter dynamical proof and an analytic proof. In the course of the dynamical proof, we prove some results on the universal compactification flow and on the generalized Bohr compactification below a given ambit which admits a left continuous semigroup operation extending the action of . The considerations around the analytic proof yield a description of the measured structure of amenable tame minimal flows, which is the second main result of this paper. We also study specializations of the above abstract topological dynamics context to model theory contexts to recover some known and to obtain some new notions and results. The main new results in the model theory contexts are: (i) a description of the Bohr compactification of the group of automorphisms of a sufficiently saturated model of a first order theory below a certain fundamental ambit associated with ; (ii) transfer of amenability of a NIP theory to amenability of the Ellis semigroup ambit; (iii) a version of Newelski's conjecture for spaces of local types with a description of Bohr compactifications below such spaces.

Consider a skew product over a topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphism , with fiber dynamics driven by a -action on a closed manifold through a cocycle . Suppose that the fiber action preserves an ergodic smooth measure of maximal entropy . Under a nondegeneracy condition called joint nontriviality, and assuming that each element is either of class or hyperbolic, we prove that admits only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy. Moreover, every such measure is of the form , where is an ergodic equilibrium state for a Hölder potential on the base. If, in addition, the fiber action is exponentially mixing of all orders, then every ergodic MME is Bernoulli, exponentially mixing of all orders, and satisfies the Central Limit Theorem. Our main novelties are entropy formulas for skew products, obtained through the cone property and -neutralized entropy, and a relative Ledrappier–Young theorem that converts the fiber entropy contribution into absolute continuity of fiberwise conditional measures. Original abstract

We establish a phase reduction and a converse realization theorem for front dynamics in one-dimensional periodic reaction-diffusion-advection equations. For sufficiently large periods under local bistability, and sufficiently small periods when the homogenized equation admits a stationary front, we construct strictly ordered invariant front families that are normally exponentially attracting and locally complete for entire orbits. Modulo spatial-period translations, the dynamics on each family reduces exactly to a circle flow: rotations correspond to propagating pulsating fronts, equilibria to stationary fronts, and connecting orbits to transition fronts between stationary fronts. Conversely, every smooth circle flow can be realized, up to time-preserving topological conjugacy, as the quotient dynamics of such a family for a periodic, locally bistable equation with constant diffusion and no advection. Realizations with a Cantor set of stationary phases and a connecting orbit in each complementary interval illustrate the richness of front dynamics in these media. We also obtain first-order phase-velocity expansions in both period limits, quantitative propagation laws near zero frozen speed, and global exponential orbital stability of propagating pulsating fronts.

Original abstract

We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence. This extends and strengthens the fixed-base temporal central limit theorem of Levin and Merzbach to the mixed-radix setting.

Original abstract

We study the maximal Lyapunov exponent of random products of positive matrices, and prove that it can be calculated to arbitrary precision with arithmetic work polynomial in the number of requested digits. In nondegenerate settings, the complexity of our method depends on the intrinsic complexity of the dynamics—which we characterize—and not on the Euclidean dimension of the ambient space in which the dynamics live. As numerical applications, we determine the Hausdorff dimension of random intersections of Sierpiński gaskets, and Viswanath's constant—the growth rate of the random Fibonacci sequence. We first establish a general inequality for nonnegative matrix families showing that, if a signed measure with finite support is sufficiently close to being stationary, then it predicts the Lyapunov exponent accurately. This framework also encompasses Pollicott's Fredholm determinant approximation. We then show that, just like drawing a constellation by picking bright stars, one can construct a sequence of signed measures approximating stationarity by picking informative orbits of the projective dynamics. Furthermore, we prove that our construction uses an asymptotically optimal number of atoms, which is governed by an intrinsic quantity we call constellation dimension.

In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention. Building on Sutner's work with de Bruijn graphs, we describe a method for deciding openness and at the same time determining n. We then introduce the notion of block-regularity of local rules as a generalization of bipermutivity and prove that it implies openness. We further identify two conditions that, together with block-regularity, ensure that every nonempty cylinder set is mapped onto the whole configuration space after a finite number of iterations, and hence that the cellular automaton is locally eventually onto. Original abstract

In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.

Original abstract

We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular -function extended from the upper half-plane to by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the -function under the linear fractional action of on . In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the -function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety – where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined – there is a point of the form with . The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of . The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax–Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouché's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.

Original abstract

We study the no deterministic images condition (NDI) for Schrödinger cocycles, which excludes a common image of a fixed probability measure under almost all projective transfer transformations. We prove two-step NDI at every energy for nonconstant measurable potentials over mixing systems and ergodic potentials with infinite essential range, and classify persistence for finite-state locally constant potentials. For bounded Markov and hidden Markov potentials on general state spaces under a one-step norm gap condition on the Markov operator, we prove Hölder bounds for solution-direction distributions above an exponential cutoff and Hölder conditional stationary measures. Counterexamples show the essential sharpness of both assumptions. For nonconstant real trigonometric potentials, including the almost Mathieu operator, we prove NDI and Hölder bounds for distributions of solution directions at all steps and all frequencies (rational or irrational). The exponent depends on the step, while the constant is uniform in steps, frequency and energy on compact intervals. For every irrational frequency and every energy with positive Lyapunov exponent, we prove non-atomicity of both Oseledets direction distributions and convergence to the unstable distribution from every phase-independent initial probability. This gives a new criterion for a zero Lyapunov exponent: a subsequential limit with an atom for one fixed initial direction suffices. All these results extend to an analytic class, with step-dependent regularity bounds.

Original abstract

In this work we consider the KAM renormalizability problem for small pseudodifferential perturbations of the semiclassical isochronous transport operator with Diophantine frequencies on the torus. Assuming that the symbol of the perturbation is real analytic and globally bounded, we prove convergence of the quantum Lindstedt series and describe completely the set of semiclassical measures and quantum limits of the renormalized system. Each of these measures is given by symplectic deformation of the Haar measure on an invariant torus for the unperturbed classical system.

Original abstract

We study the three classical integrable generalized cubic Hénon–Heiles systems – Kaup–Kupershmidt, KdV, and Sawada–Kotera – from the viewpoint of bi-Hamiltonian geometry and separation of variables. On the standard symplectic manifold , we construct compatible Poisson deformations , compute the associated recursion operators , and analyze the action of on the codistribution generated by the first integrals. This yields the corresponding control matrices, whose eigenvalues provide the separating coordinates. For the generalized Kaup–Kupershmidt case we carry out the construction explicitly: we determine a deformation vector field, the compatible Poisson tensor, the torsionless recursion operator, the control matrix, the separating coordinates, and, crucially, the conjugate momenta. We then derive the separated relations and write the Hamilton equations in canonical separated variables, thus decomposing the original Hamiltonian system into two separated subsystems. To the best of our knowledge, this explicit derivation of the separating variables and, in particular, of the conjugate momenta for the generalized Kaup–Kupershmidt system is new. For the KdV and Sawada–Kotera cases we show how the same bi-Hamiltonian scheme applies, emphasizing both the common geometric mechanism and the features peculiar to each system. In this way, the three generalized cubic Hénon–Heiles systems are treated within a unified framework based on compatible Poisson structures, recursion operators, control matrices, and Darboux–Nijenhuis coordinates.

Original abstract

Let be an integer and let be the Liouville function. In 1965, Chowla gave a conjecture that the values of are asymptotically unrelated for any distinct natural numbers . In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will show a dynamical generalization of Chowla's conjecture on average. In the proof, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. Moreover, we will use this approach to show an analogue of the dynamical Chowla's conjecture along the primes on average. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and a variant for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.
